Per-token normalised time, honouring an already-normalised column

Source: R/time_norm.R
resolve_time_norm.Rd

Builds the [0, 1] time axis the modelling functions fit on. By default (time_normalised = "auto") the column and its name are passed to time_already_normalised(): a column that is already proportional is used as-is (clamped to [0, 1]); anything else is rescaled to [0, 1] within each token, from its first f0 to its last when f0 is given.

Usage

resolve_time_norm(
  data,
  time,
  token,
  time_normalised = c("auto", "no", "yes"),
  quiet = FALSE,
  f0 = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the time and token columns.

time

Name of the time column.

token

Name of the token-ID column.

time_normalised

One of "auto" (default; detect and use an already-normalised column as-is), "no" (always rescale per token), or "yes" (declare the column already normalised to [0, 1]; values outside that interval are an error).

quiet

Suppress the message emitted when auto-detection decides the column is already normalised. Default FALSE.

f0

Name of the f0 column, or NULL (the default). With f0, the rescale runs from each token's first f0 to its last; without it, from each token's first row to its last.

Value

A list with time_norm (numeric vector, one value per row of data) and prenormalised (logical: was the column used as-is?). A missing time, token or f0 column is an error.

Details

In the rescaling path with f0, each token runs from its first f0 (0) to its last f0 (1), as in normalise_time_token(). Rows have f0 as there: a row has f0 when its f0 value is a number, and in a column in Hz (one that hz_f0_columns() finds) 0 is no f0. A column with negative markers, such as -1, is not read as Hz, so those values count as f0: set them to NA first (see suggest_unvoiced()). Rows before the first f0 or after the last get NA, so rows without f0 at a token's edges do not move the axis, and removing them changes nothing. A token whose f0 is all at one time gets 0.5 on the rows at that time, and a token with no f0 gets NA. Rows with an NA token form one token of their own, as in the rescale without f0. fit_gca(), fit_gamm(), fit_polynomial() and compute_mean_contour() pass their f0 column.

Without f0, each token runs from its first row with a time to its last, rows without f0 included. A token whose times are all the same gets 0.5 on every row, rows with no time included. Other NA times stay NA. On data with no rows without f0 at the token edges, the two rescales are the same.

In "auto" mode, a <tier>_t01, token_t01 or time_prop column whose values all lie in [0, 1] is used as it is, whatever rows it has left, so removing rows does not switch it to the rescale. Columns made by normalise_time_token() and normalise_time_landmarks() already run from the first f0 to the last. On time_prop, a column made by an older version or a subset taken after a column was made, the f0 may not reach 0 or 1. A <tier>_tseq or <tier>_tbound column is judged by its values only, so one that spans several segments is rescaled per token here; for tokens with the same number of segments the boundaries then sit at 1/n, 2/n and so on. A token whose first or last segment has no values on the axis is stretched: its other segments fill 0 to 1. On a <tier>_tseq that is a segment with f0 at fewer than two times; on a <tier>_tbound, one with no f0. (fit_gamm() keeps a <tier>_tseq or <tier>_tbound on its own scale instead.)

See also

time_already_normalised() for the detection rule.
